title: Sports Events Timeline
description: Place legendary sports moments and achievements in their correct chronological order.

share.title: Sports Events Timeline
share.description: Can you place these legendary sports moments in the correct chronological order?

seo.title: Sports Events Timeline Quiz - Historic Moments Game
seo.description: Play a free online sports timeline quiz. Guess the order of legendary sports milestones, from the first World Cup to Usain Bolt's record, and build a streak.

items.label: Inaugural FA Cup Final
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Wanderers F.C. defeats Royal Engineers 1-0 in the first-ever FA Cup final at the Kennington Oval.

items.label: First Wimbledon Championship
items.subtitle: London, England
items.description: Spencer Gore wins the inaugural gentlemen's singles championship, defeating William Marshall.

items.label: First Modern Olympic Games
items.subtitle: Athens, Greece
items.description: The Olympic Games are officially reborn in Athens, featuring 241 athletes from 14 nations.

items.label: First Boston Marathon
items.subtitle: Boston, USA
items.description: John J. McDermott wins the first running of the oldest annual marathon in the world.

items.label: First Tour de France
items.subtitle: France
items.description: Maurice Garin wins the inaugural six-stage bicycle race, covering 2,428 kilometers.

items.label: First Modern World Series
items.subtitle: Boston, USA
items.description: The Boston Americans defeat the Pittsburgh Pirates in the first modern championship series of Major League Baseball.

items.label: First Stanley Cup of NHL Era
items.subtitle: Toronto, Canada
items.description: The Toronto Arenas win the first Stanley Cup championship after the founding of the National Hockey League.

items.label: First FIFA World Cup
items.subtitle: Montevideo, Uruguay
items.description: Uruguay defeats Argentina 4-2 in the final to win the first-ever FIFA World Cup.

items.label: Babe Didrikson Wins Two Golds
items.subtitle: Los Angeles Olympics
items.description: Mildred 'Babe' Didrikson wins gold in javelin and 80m hurdles, and silver in the high jump.

items.label: Jesse Owens Wins 4 Gold Medals
items.subtitle: Berlin, Germany
items.description: African-American athlete Jesse Owens wins four gold medals, defying Nazi racial theories.

items.label: Jackie Robinson Breaks Color Barrier
items.subtitle: Brooklyn, New York, USA
items.description: Robinson starts at first base for the Brooklyn Dodgers, ending racial segregation in Major League Baseball.

items.label: Don Bradman Retires
items.subtitle: The Oval, London
items.description: The legendary Australian cricketer is bowled for a duck in his final innings, finishing with a career average of 99.94.

items.label: First Formula 1 Championship Race
items.subtitle: Silverstone, United Kingdom
items.description: Giuseppe Farina wins the British Grand Prix, the first official race of the new Formula One World Championship.

items.label: Bannister Breaks 4-Minute Mile
items.subtitle: Oxford, United Kingdom
items.description: Roger Bannister becomes the first person to run a mile in under four minutes, finishing in 3:59.4.

items.label: Pelé Wins First World Cup
items.subtitle: Solna, Sweden
items.description: A teenage Pelé (age 17) scores twice in the final to lead Brazil to victory over Sweden.

items.label: Wilt Chamberlain Scores 100 Points
items.subtitle: Hershey, Pennsylvania, USA
items.description: Chamberlain sets the NBA single-game scoring record as the Philadelphia Warriors defeat the New York Knicks.

items.label: Muhammad Ali Beats Sonny Liston
items.subtitle: Miami Beach, Florida, USA
items.description: Cassius Clay (later Muhammad Ali) wins the World Heavyweight Championship after Liston retires on his stool.

items.label: England Wins the World Cup
items.subtitle: Wembley Stadium, London
items.description: England defeats West Germany 4-2 after extra time, marked by Geoff Hurst's famous hat-trick.

items.label: First Super Bowl Played
items.subtitle: Los Angeles, California, USA
items.description: The Green Bay Packers of the NFL defeat the Kansas City Chiefs of the AFL 35-10 in the first Championship Game.

items.label: Bob Beamon's Historic Jump
items.subtitle: Mexico City Olympics
items.description: Beamon shatters the world record by 55 cm with a jump of 8.90 meters, which stood for 23 years.

items.label: Arthur Ashe Wins US Open
items.subtitle: Forest Hills, New York, USA
items.description: Ashe becomes the first Black man to win a Grand Slam singles title, defeating Tom Okker in the final.

items.label: Mark Spitz Wins 7 Gold Medals
items.subtitle: Munich, West Germany
items.description: American swimmer Mark Spitz wins seven gold medals, setting a world record in every single event.

items.label: Battle of the Sexes Tennis Match
items.subtitle: Houston, Texas, USA
items.description: Billie Jean King defeats Bobby Riggs in straight sets, a milestone for women's sports and equality.

items.label: The Rumble in the Jungle
items.subtitle: Kinshasa, Zaire
items.description: Muhammad Ali defeats George Foreman using his 'rope-a-dope' strategy to regain the heavyweight title.

items.label: The Thrilla in Manila
items.subtitle: Manila, Philippines
items.description: Muhammad Ali defeats Joe Frazier in their brutal third and final bout after Frazier's trainer stops the fight.

items.label: Nadia Comăneci Scores Perfect 10
items.subtitle: Montreal, Canada
items.description: The 14-year-old Romanian gymnast receives the first-ever perfect 10.0 score on the uneven bars.

items.label: NBA Triple Overtime Finals Game
items.subtitle: Boston, Massachusetts, USA
items.description: The Boston Celtics defeat the Phoenix Suns in a triple-overtime thriller in Game 5 of the Finals.

items.label: Miracle on Ice
items.subtitle: Lake Placid, New York, USA
items.description: A team of US college players pulls off a monumental upset, defeating the dominant Soviet Olympic hockey team.

items.label: Borg defeats McEnroe in Epic Final
items.subtitle: Wimbledon, London
items.description: Björn Borg wins his fifth consecutive Wimbledon title in a five-set match famous for its 18-16 tiebreaker.

items.label: First Athletics World Championships
items.subtitle: Helsinki, Finland
items.description: The first-ever World Championships in Athletics are held, separate from the Olympic Games.

items.label: Maradona's Hand of God Goal
items.subtitle: Mexico City, Mexico
items.description: Diego Maradona scores two iconic goals against England (Hand of God and Goal of the Century) in the World Cup.

items.label: Ben Johnson Stripped of Gold
items.subtitle: Seoul, South Korea
items.description: Canadian sprinter Ben Johnson is stripped of his 100m gold medal after testing positive for anabolic steroids.

items.label: Steffi Graf Wins Golden Slam
items.subtitle: Seoul Olympics & Slams
items.description: Graf becomes the only tennis player to win all four Grand Slam singles titles and Olympic gold in the same calendar year.

items.label: Florence Griffith-Joyner 100m Record
items.subtitle: Indianapolis, USA
items.description: Flo-Jo runs the 100m in an astonishing, still-unbroken world record time of 10.49 seconds.

items.label: Jordan Wins First NBA Championship
items.subtitle: Chicago, Illinois, USA
items.description: The Chicago Bulls defeat the Los Angeles Lakers in the Finals, starting Michael Jordan's first championship run.

items.label: Barcelona Olympics Dream Team
items.subtitle: Barcelona, Spain
items.description: The first USA Olympic basketball team to feature active NBA superstars cruises to the gold medal.

items.label: Denmark's Miracle Euro Triumph
items.subtitle: Gothenburg, Sweden
items.description: Denmark, who failed to qualify and were only invited after Yugoslavia's exclusion, win the European Championship.

items.label: Fatal Crash of Ayrton Senna
items.subtitle: Imola, Italy
items.description: Three-time Formula One World Champion Ayrton Senna dies after crashing at the San Marino Grand Prix.

items.label: Michael Jordan's 'Flu Game'
items.subtitle: Salt Lake City, Utah, USA
items.description: Jordan scores 38 points in Game 5 of the NBA Finals despite battling severe dehydration and flu-like symptoms.

items.label: Tiger Woods Wins Masters by 12
items.subtitle: Augusta, Georgia, USA
items.description: At age 21, Tiger Woods becomes the youngest and first non-white golfer to win the Masters by a record margin.

items.label: France Wins First World Cup
items.subtitle: Saint-Denis, France
items.description: Zinedine Zidane scores twice as host nation France defeats Brazil 3-0 in the final.

items.label: Brandi Chastain's Celebration
items.subtitle: Pasadena, California, USA
items.description: Chastain scores the winning penalty for the USA in the Women's World Cup and celebrates in iconic fashion.

items.label: Schumacher Wins Ferrari Title
items.subtitle: Suzuka, Japan
items.description: Michael Schumacher wins the Japanese GP to secure Ferrari's first Drivers' Championship in 21 years.

items.label: Goran Ivanišević Wins Wimbledon
items.subtitle: Wimbledon, London
items.description: Ranked 125th, Ivanišević becomes the first-ever wildcard to win a Grand Slam singles title.

items.label: Roger Federer Wins First Grand Slam
items.subtitle: Wimbledon, London
items.description: Federer defeats Mark Philippoussis to win Wimbledon, launching his decade-long era of dominance.

items.label: Greece's Shock Euro Triumph
items.subtitle: Lisbon, Portugal
items.description: Underdog Greece pulls off one of the greatest surprises in football history by defeating Portugal 1-0 in the final.

items.label: The Miracle of Istanbul
items.subtitle: Istanbul, Turkey
items.description: Liverpool recovers from 3-0 down at half-time to defeat AC Milan on penalties in the Champions League final.

items.label: Zidane Headbutt in World Cup Final
items.subtitle: Berlin, Germany
items.description: Zinedine Zidane is red-carded in his final professional match for headbutting Marco Materazzi, and Italy wins the cup.

items.label: Michael Phelps Wins 8 Golds
items.subtitle: Beijing, China
items.description: Phelps wins eight gold medals, breaking Mark Spitz's 1972 record for most gold medals in a single Olympics.

items.label: Usain Bolt Runs 9.58 Seconds
items.subtitle: Berlin, Germany
items.description: Usain Bolt sets the still-unbroken 100m world record at the World Athletics Championships.

items.label: Federer wins 77-Game Final
items.subtitle: Wimbledon, London
items.description: Roger Federer defeats Andy Roddick 16-14 in the fifth set to win his 15th Grand Slam, surpassing Pete Sampras.

items.label: Longest Tennis Match Ever Played
items.subtitle: Wimbledon, London
items.description: John Isner defeats Nicolas Mahut in a match lasting 11 hours and 5 minutes over three days (70-68 in the fifth set).

items.label: Spain Wins First World Cup
items.subtitle: Johannesburg, South Africa
items.description: Andrés Iniesta scores in the 116th minute to lead Spain to a 1-0 victory over the Netherlands.

items.label: Japan Wins Women's World Cup
items.subtitle: Frankfurt, Germany
items.description: Japan defeats the USA on penalties, becoming the first Asian nation to win a FIFA World Cup.

items.label: Lance Armstrong Stripped of Titles
items.subtitle: Austin, Texas, USA
items.description: The US Anti-Doping Agency disqualifies Armstrong from all his 7 Tour de France wins due to systemic doping.

items.label: Team GB Super Saturday
items.subtitle: London, United Kingdom
items.description: Great Britain wins three gold medals in athletics within 44 minutes through Ennis, Rutherford, and Farah.

items.label: Germany Defeats Brazil 7-1
items.subtitle: Belo Horizonte, Brazil
items.description: Germany inflicts the heaviest defeat ever on a World Cup host, scoring five goals in the first 29 minutes.

items.label: Leicester City Wins Premier League
items.subtitle: Leicester, United Kingdom
items.description: Underdogs Leicester City complete the most improbable title run in English football history at 5000-1 odds.

items.label: Michael Phelps Retires with 28 Medals
items.subtitle: Rio de Janeiro, Brazil
items.description: Phelps wins his final gold medal at the Rio Olympics, cementing his record as the most decorated Olympian of all time.

items.label: Patriots' 25-Point Comeback
items.subtitle: Houston, Texas, USA
items.description: Tom Brady leads the Patriots back from a 28-3 deficit to defeat the Atlanta Falcons 34-28 in overtime.

items.label: Eliud Kipchoge Sub-2-Hour Marathon
items.subtitle: Vienna, Austria
items.description: Kipchoge becomes the first person to run a marathon distance in under two hours, clocking 1:59:40 in a special event.

items.label: Lewis Hamilton Equals Schumacher Record
items.subtitle: Istanbul, Turkey
items.description: Hamilton wins the Turkish Grand Prix to secure his seventh Formula 1 World Championship, matching Michael Schumacher.

items.label: Lionel Messi Wins World Cup
items.subtitle: Lusail, Qatar
items.description: Messi leads Argentina to victory over France on penalties in one of the greatest finals in World Cup history.

items.label: LeBron James NBA Scoring Record
items.subtitle: Los Angeles, California, USA
items.description: LeBron James surpasses Kareem Abdul-Jabbar's career record of 38,387 points.

items.label: Novak Djokovic Wins 24th Slam
items.subtitle: New York City, USA
items.description: Djokovic defeats Daniil Medvedev at the US Open, tying Margaret Court for the most singles majors in tennis history.

items.label: Haaland Single-Season Goal Record
items.subtitle: Manchester, England
items.description: Erling Haaland scores his 36th league goal of the season for Manchester City, breaking the 38-game era record.

items.label: Coco Gauff Wins First Slam
items.subtitle: New York City, USA
items.description: The 19-year-old American defeats Aryna Sabalenka in the US Open final.

items.label: Kansas City Chiefs Back-to-Back
items.subtitle: Las Vegas, Nevada, USA
items.description: Patrick Mahomes leads the Chiefs to an overtime victory against the San Francisco 49ers in Super Bowl LVIII.

items.label: Tadej Pogačar Tour & Giro Double
items.subtitle: Nice, France / Rome, Italy
items.description: Pogačar becomes the first cyclist since Marco Pantani in 1998 to win both Grand Tours in the same season.

items.label: Simone Biles Wins 3 Golds in Paris
items.subtitle: Paris, France
items.description: Biles dominates the gymnastics events, completing her comeback and bringing her total Olympic golds to 7.
